name: Baalis
title: King of the Ammonites
summary: Baalis was the king of the Ammonites at the time of Jerusalem's fall and the Babylonian exile. He is known for orchestrating the conspiracy that led to the murder of Gedaliah, the Babylonian-appointed governor over Judah. His actions contributed to further destabilization of the Jewish remnant in the land after Jerusalem's destruction.

keyEvents.title: The Conspiracy Against Gedaliah
keyEvents.description: Baalis, the king of Ammon, sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to kill Gedaliah, who had been appointed by Nebuchadnezzar as governor over those remaining in Judah.

keyEvents.title: Warning About the Assassination Plot
keyEvents.description: Johanan son of Kareah warned Gedaliah that Baalis had sent Ishmael to take his life, but Gedaliah refused to believe the warning.

keyEvents.title: The Murder of Gedaliah
keyEvents.description: Ishmael son of Nethaniah carried out Baalis' plan and killed Gedaliah in Mizpah along with the Jews and Babylonians who were there. This led to further chaos among the Jewish remnant.

keyEvents.title: Ishmael's Flight to Ammon
keyEvents.description: After the murder of Gedaliah and subsequent atrocities, Ishmael fled with eight of his men to the Ammonites, back to his employer Baalis.

keyEvents.title: Consequences for the Jewish Remnant
keyEvents.description: As a result of Baalis' conspiracy and the murder of Gedaliah, the remaining Jewish population fled to Egypt out of fear of Babylonian retribution, despite the prophet Jeremiah's warnings.
